slides.title: cody.dev Cody is a coding AI assistant https://code.dev
slides.text: cody.dev Cody is a coding AI assistant https://code.dev https://sourcegraph.com/cody You can run it as VS Code extension By default it uses GPT-4 Free (limited bandwidth or $9/mo paid) But you can also use it with a local model, for example Ollama running CodeLlama ( ollama run codellama:7b-code ) Go to extension settings "Cody > Autocomplete > Advanced: Provider" and select "unstable-ollama" from the drop-down list. Very good step-by-step demo: installation and usage https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gY_E3QBZ-NE In your code you can write comments on the code - and Cody will write the code for you. Or you can click on the yellow circle "Asl Cody to Generate" - and type your instructions. Writing code, Autocomplete, Generating unit tests, chat (with online LLMs), write comments, documentation, descriptions, follow instructions to edit code, etc. etc.

RAGatouille - Easily use & train SOT retrieval methods in any RAG pipeline (using ColBERT). https://github.com/bclavie/RAGatouille https://til.simonwillison.net/llms/colbert-ragatouille ColBERT is designed to scale to large document collections and can handle millions of docs efficiently. It uses Efficient indexing & retrieval (top-k most similar documents) ColBERT is good for ad-hoc retrieval, but not as good for question answering, summarization, and text classification Late Interaction: first encode the query and doc, then compute the similarity between the embeddings at the token level (MaxSim scoring). The final similarity score is the sum of the token-wise similarities.

slides.title: How quantized 4bit models run? Suppose that weights
slides.text: How quantized 4bit models run? Suppose that weights are stored as 4bit. Embedding vectors and activations are typically kept at higher precision (8bit or 16bit). Ways to do multiplication: Full Conversion to higher precision . Both weights and activations are temporarily converted to a higher precision (e.g., 16-bit or 32-bit) before multiplication. Partial Conversion with scaling. Weights remain in 4-bit format, activations converted to a higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) but scaled down before multiplication (to avoid overflow while maintaining some dynamic range). Drawback - reduced accuracy. Native Low-Bit Multiplication (if supported by hardware) : both weights and activations keep their accuracy (4bit and 8bit). NF4 is used only for storage. You need to de-quantize values before using them. Absmax Quantization to 8 bit If M = max(abs(your data)), c = (127/M), then x -> c*x will project float numbers (x) into range (-127,+127) Quantile  Quantization to 4 bit Sort your data points in ascending order and divide them into 16 parts (quantiles) containing equal number of points. This maps original values to 16 4-bit values. But it is a slow (sorting, finding levels). Normalized float4 (NF4) quantization - a Quantile  Quantization using pre-calculated quantiles (for Gaussian distribution) https://ai.plainenglish.io/qlora-key-quantization-and-fine-tuning-techniques-in-the-era-of-large-language-models-0fa05a961d27

slides.title: Why Do LLM Hallucinate ? Why Do LLM
slides.text: Why Do LLM Hallucinate ? Why Do LLM Hallucinate ? LLM predicts the next token based on statistics of training data. LLM doesn't have brains. LLM doesn't have judgement. If the right data was not available in training, or if training data was noisy, LLM will try to select from what it has, and it may go in a completely wrong direction.  This is hallucination. LLM does not understand, it simply follows contextual patterns. Good prompts may help to avoid hallucinations.  You can also use separate LLM Agent(s). LLM Hallucinations in RAG QA https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lsZCVmCBRlc https://www.holisticai.com/blog/types-of-llm-hallucinations

slides.title: Attention = Facilitation and Inhibition Attention in Transformer
slides.text: Attention = Facilitation and Inhibition Attention in Transformer architecture implements both facilitation (Attention Matrix) and lateral Inhibition (Softmax normalization). Similar mechanisms exist in the brain. "Neurons that fire together, wire together" is a quote by neuropsychologist Donald Hebb. Hebb first used the phrase in 1949 to describe how brain pathways are formed and reinforced through repetition. - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_facilitation Lateral Inhibition - the ability of an excited neuron to reduce the activity of its neighbors. It prevents the lateral spread of neuronal activity, which creates an increased contrast in excitation between neighboring neurons. This allows better sensory acuity.  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateral_inhibition Attention in Psychology, Neuroscience, and Machine Learning https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7177153/ Donald Hebb Softmax function a.k.a. normalized exponential function Airy Disk (George Biddell Airy) Point spread functions
